domain: Arithmetic with rational numbers (subtracting fractions and mixed numbers)

skills.name: Convert mixed numbers to improper fractions
skills.definition: Rewrite a mixed number as an equivalent improper fraction by converting the whole part into fractional units (whole × denominator) and adding the numerator.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts a mixed number (e.g., 3 1/2) into an improper fraction (e.g., 7/2).
A step rewrites a mixed number as whole + fraction and then combines into a single fraction.
exclusion_criteria: Only rewriting a whole number as a fraction with a chosen denominator (use S03).
Only converting an improper fraction to a mixed number/whole number (use S06).

skills.name: Find and use a common denominator (LCM/scaling)
skills.definition: Determine a common denominator for two fractions (often via LCM) and create equivalent fractions by scaling numerators and denominators.
inclusion_criteria: A step states or implies finding a common denominator/LCM.
A step converts one or both fractions to equivalent forms with the same denominator by multiplying numerator and denominator.
exclusion_criteria: Denominators are already equal and the step directly subtracts numerators (use S04).
Only rewriting an integer as a fraction with a target denominator (use S03).

skills.name: Rewrite a whole number as an equivalent fraction
skills.definition: Express an integer as an equivalent fraction with a specified denominator to enable fraction operations (e.g., 3 = 15/5).
inclusion_criteria: A step rewrites an integer as k/k or as an equivalent fraction with a target denominator (e.g., 2 = 16/8, 4 = 12/3).
exclusion_criteria: Converting a mixed number to an improper fraction (use S01).
Finding a common denominator between two non-integer fractions (use S02).

skills.name: Subtract fractions using a common denominator
skills.definition: Compute the difference of two fractions by subtracting numerators over a shared denominator (including the already-same-denominator case).
inclusion_criteria: A step performs subtraction in the form a/b − c/b = (a−c)/b.
A step subtracts after expressing both quantities with the same denominator (whether by S02/S03 or already equal).
exclusion_criteria: The step is only about finding/creating the common denominator (use S02 or S03).
The step is only simplifying/reducing the resulting fraction (use S05).

skills.name: Simplify a fraction to lowest terms
skills.definition: Reduce a fraction by dividing numerator and denominator by a common factor and/or recognizing when it is already in lowest terms.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly reduces a fraction (e.g., −3/12 = −1/4).
A step states the fraction is already in lowest terms.
exclusion_criteria: Only converting between mixed and improper forms without reduction (use S01 or S06).
Only performing the subtraction arithmetic (use S04).

skills.name: Convert an improper fraction to a mixed number (or whole number)
skills.definition: Rewrite an improper fraction as a mixed number (or integer) by dividing the numerator by the denominator and expressing the remainder as a fraction.
inclusion_criteria: A step explicitly converts an improper fraction to a mixed number (e.g., 7/4 = 1 3/4).
A step identifies an improper fraction equals a whole number (e.g., 3/3 = 1).
exclusion_criteria: Only simplifying a fraction without expressing it as a mixed number/whole number (use S05).

skills.name: Subtract mixed numbers by separating whole and fractional parts
skills.definition: Compute a mixed-number difference by subtracting whole parts and fractional parts and recombining (including cases where the fractional difference is negative).
inclusion_criteria: A step sets up subtraction as (whole difference) + (fraction difference), e.g., (4−2) + (4/12−7/12).
A step recombines the whole and fractional results into a single value.
exclusion_criteria: The method is to convert mixed numbers to improper fractions first (use S01 then S04).
Only subtracting two fractions without whole parts (use S04).
